reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis misinterprets the research question by proposing a processing route to increase hardness/strength rather than explaining why the equimolar solid-solution state has low hardness/strength, and the stated 'addition of 4.2 at.% Cr' contradicts the starting equimolar composition.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification test only checks whether a high hardness is achieved, not whether the hypothesized mechanisms (grain boundary, dislocation, solid solution strengthening) govern the low strength of the simple solid-solution state, so it does not test the stated hypothesis.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis does not address the core question of what governs the low hardness/strength in the equimolar solid-solution state and instead describes a separate processing study, making it not useful for a researcher investigating the deformation behavior of the starting material.
